stories.title: Rahul Gandhi celebrates his 56th birthday at Congress headquarter:Party workers depict him as 'Lord Parshuram' in Varanasi, pour milk over photograph
stories.summary: Birthday wishes poured in from across the political spectrum, for the Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi as he turned 56 on Friday. Gandhi arrived at the Congress headquarters to celebrate his birthday with party workers, accompanied by his sister and Party national general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. PM Narendra Modi, Congress party president Mallikarjun Kharge and several leaders of the INDIA bloc and BJP extended their wishes for Gandhi. Posters celebrating Rahul Gandhi's birthday were displayed outside the Congress headquarters, Indira Bhawan, in Delhi. In Varanasi, Congress workers performed special rituals and offered prayers in his honour. Congress workers perform rituals in the middle of the Ganga On Friday, Congress workers travelled by boat to the middle of the River Ganga in Varanasi. They carried a waterproof cut-out depicting Rahul Gandhi in the form of Lord Parshuram. In the cut-out, Rahul Gandhi was shown holding an axe in one hand and a copy of the Constitution of India in the other. Workers performed a Rudrabhishek accompanied by Vedic chants. They also cut an 11-kg laddu cake and prayed for Rahul Gandhi's long, healthy and successful life. See photos- Youth Congress leader explains symbolism behind the celebration Youth Congress district president Vikas Singh said Rahul Gandhi consistently stands against what he described as anti-democratic forces, corruption and those who disregard the Constitution. He said Rahul Gandhi continues to fight for democratic values, social justice and constitutional principles, while raising the voice of ordinary citizens. According to Singh, Rahul Gandhi symbolises struggle and resistance. Drawing a parallel with Lord Parshuram, he said that just as Parshuram destroyed evil and oppression, Rahul Gandhi would challenge those who oppose democratic values and constitutional principles. ‘Politics should serve the last person in society’ Vikas Singh further said Rahul Gandhi's politics is not limited to gaining power but is rooted in ensuring justice and rights reach the last person in society. He said the birthday celebrations were organised in the spirit of service, commitment and prayer. Expressing his personal aspiration, Singh said Congress workers hoped Rahul Gandhi would become Prime Minister after the next general election. He added that this sentiment was the reason behind portraying him in the form of Lord Parshuram, noting that India is a democratic country where everyone has the freedom to express their views. PM Modi and other leaders extend birthday wishes Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted on X: Birthday greetings to Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi Ji. I wish him good health and a long life. M. K. Stalin said Rahul Gandhi has consistently spoken for national progress, democratic values and the welfare of all sections of society. He wished him good health and a long life. Telangana CM Revanth Reddy said Rahul Gandhi's commitment to democratic values, social justice and public welfare continues to inspire many people. Congress General Secretary K. C. Venugopal said that at a time when the country faces challenges relating to democracy and the Constitution, Rahul Gandhi has emerged as a strong voice for an inclusive and democratic India. He described him as a source of hope for young people, the poor and marginalised communities. Sanjay Raut wished Rahul Gandhi good health, happiness and continued strength in public service, expressing hope that the coming year would bring him success and fulfilment. | Rahul Gandhi celebrates 56th birthday: From ₹11 crore properties ₹3.81 crore in mutual funds, lets decode how RaGa invests Rahul Gandhi worked under a different name for three years Rahul Gandhi was born on 19 June 1970 in New Delhi. He is the son of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and former Congress president Sonia Gandhi. He is the elder of two siblings, with Priyanka Gandhi being younger. He began his schooling at Modern School before moving to The Doon School. Following the assassination of Indira Gandhi in 1984, security concerns forced him to continue his education from home. In 1989, he enrolled at St. Stephen's College, but again had to discontinue his studies because of security concerns. He later moved to the United States and joined Harvard University. However, after Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991, he left Harvard due to security issues. Rahul subsequently enrolled at Rollins College, graduating with a degree in Arts in 1994. During his time in Florida, his identity was reportedly known only to university authorities and security personnel. In 1995, he completed an MPhil degree from Trinity College Cambridge in the United Kingdom. Career before politics After completing his studies, Rahul Gandhi worked for three years in London with the management consulting firm Monitor Group. Due to security concerns, his identity was kept confidential and he reportedly worked under the name "Raul Vinci". He returned to India in 2002 and became a director of Mumbai-based technology outsourcing company Backops Services Private Limited. Rahul Gandhi formally entered politics in March 2004, beginning a political career that would eventually see him become Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

stories.title: ₹2 crore Hapur robbery accused killed in encounter:Looted cash and jewellery from businessman's family; carried a reward of ₹50,000
stories.summary: A key accused in the high-profile Hapur robbery case, in which a businessman's family was held hostage and valuables worth nearly ₹2 crore were looted, was killed in a police encounter late on Thursday night. The accused, identified as Shyam (28), carried a reward of ₹50,000 on his head. During the exchange of fire, Head Constable Manoj Kumar also sustained a gunshot injury. According to Superintendent of Police (SP) KG Singh, the encounter took place at around 10:30 pm during a vehicle-checking operation on Bulandshahr Road under the Hapur Nagar police station area. Accused opened fire after being cornered SP KG Singh said a suspicious motorcyclist attempted to flee after spotting the police. Officers pursued him and alerted Hapur Dehat police. A joint police team eventually surrounded the suspect near Godi village. Realising he was trapped, the accused allegedly took cover behind a tubewell and opened fire on the police team. Officers retaliated, and Shyam was critically injured in the exchange. He was rushed to a government hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Mastermind and gang members arrested earlier Earlier, on 7 June, police arrested five members of the gang following a major encounter on Sultanpur Road. Among those arrested was suspended Uttar Pradesh Police constable Vicky Gautam, who police identified as the mastermind behind the robbery. Multiple criminal cases registered against Shyam The deceased accused, Shyam, son of Virendra, was a resident of Surajpur village under Patwai police station in Rampur district. Police said he was wanted in the Hapur robbery case registered on 1 June and had several criminal cases against him, including charges under the Gangster Act, robbery and dacoity. At least four such cases were registered in districts including Moradabad. First, see the pictures- How was the robbery carried out? The robbery took place on 2 June at the residence of businessman Narendra Agarwal. His 17-year-old grandson, Siddhant, had returned home early from a business trip. According to investigators, the robbers had already been waiting nearby. As soon as Siddhant entered the house, four to five armed men followed him inside. The criminals allegedly pointed a pistol at his head before taking businessman Narendra Agarwal, his wife Sushila Agarwal and the household watchman hostage. The gang demanded ₹2 crore in cash. When the businessman said such an amount was not available in the house, the robbers tied up all family members and the watchman using bedsheets. They confined them to a room and spent nearly an hour searching the property. The gang eventually escaped with approximately 1.25 kg of gold jewellery, silver ornaments and cash worth several lakh rupees from cupboards and lockers. After the robbers fled, the family alerted police. Senior officers, including the DIG and SP, arrived at the scene and launched an investigation. CCTV footage from the surrounding area was examined. CCTV footage led to identification The robbery sparked outrage among traders across Hapur. Business associations questioned the law-and-order situation and gave police a 72-hour ultimatum to crack the case, warning of market closures and protests if no progress was made. During the investigation, police recovered CCTV footage from a location around 150 metres from Narendra Agarwal's residence. The footage showed three suspects fleeing on a motorcycle carrying a bag shortly after the robbery. The images helped investigators identify the accused. How police arrested the gang ? Circle Officer (CO) Varun Mishra said that on the night of 7 June, police teams were conducting checks on Sultanpur Road in the Kotwali Dehat area when they spotted five suspicious men riding two motorcycles. When officers attempted to stop them, the suspects accelerated and allegedly opened fire. Police returned fire, injuring Rohit and Shahbe Alam. The area was cordoned off and five accused were arrested. Those arrested were- Cash, Jewellery and Weapons Recovered Police recovered- Gang conducted reconnaissance for four months Investigators found that the gang had conducted detailed surveillance of the businessman's residence before carrying out the robbery. Initially, police believed the reconnaissance had lasted two months. Further investigation revealed the criminals had monitored the house and its occupants for nearly four months. They gathered information on visitors, security arrangements, family routines, the number of people present in the house and even the location of the safe. Police also arrested Guddu of Moradabad and Tinkoo of Sambhal in connection with the case. According to investigators, Tinkoo's father, Satpal, worked as a mason for the businessman for several months. Police claim Tinkoo supplied crucial information regarding the location of the safe and where its key was kept. Investigators believe this is why the robbers were able to go directly to the places where cash and valuables were stored. Suspended constable had criminal history Vicky Gautam, the alleged mastermind, is originally from Amroha and joined the Uttar Pradesh Police in 2016. He was posted in Sitapur until 2024 but was suspended after remaining absent from duty for ten days without authorisation. Police records show he had previously been jailed in criminal cases. On 19 May 2025, he was arrested in Moradabad's Dilari police station area with old currency notes worth approximately ₹1.5 crore. Investigators also discovered that Vicky Gautam and Tinkoo became acquainted while serving time in jail, a connection that later played a key role in planning and executing the Hapur robbery.

stories.title: Is Akhilesh's Samajwadi Party heading for a split?:21 MPs reject Rajbhar's claim saying 'only those with something to hide would leave'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has claimed that the Samajwadi Party (SP) is heading towards a major split. To verify the claim, Dainik Bhaskar contacted all 37 SP MPs elected to the Lok Sabha. Of the 37 MPs, 16 did not respond to calls, while 21 spoke to the newspaper. They were asked two questions- Most MPs rejected Rajbhar's allegation outright, describing him as a political showman who makes controversial statements for publicity. Several said there was no dissatisfaction within the party and that no MP was considering leaving SP. Rajbhar's claim: Dalit, OBC and General category MPs ready to leave Rajbhar alleged that SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav had submitted a list of names to Union Home Minister Amit Shah and suggested that several SP MPs were ready to switch sides. According to Rajbhar, most Dalit, OBC and General category MPs from Purvanchal, excluding Muslim and Yadav MPs, were prepared to leave the Samajwadi Party. SP won 37 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 General Election, including 17 seats in Purvanchal- Among them, Ghazipur is represented by Afzal Ansari, while Azamgarh is represented by Dharmendra Yadav. Purvanchal MPs reject Rajbhar's allegations Pushpendra Saroj (Kaushambi)- Rajbhar should first look after his own party. Let him tell us how many MLAs remain with him. BJP has been trying to lure us for years. Only those who are afraid change sides. We are not leaving SP." Rajeev Rai (Ghosi)- Rajbhar has developed a habit of boasting. It has become incurable. He is making such statements out of desperation over securing tickets for his sons. The question of SP MPs joining BJP does not arise. Daroga Prasad Saroj (Lalganj)- Only a thief would leave SP. He must be involved in some sort of brokerage. The national president respected everyone and gave them opportunities. Everything else is false. Ram Prasad Chaudhary (Basti)- That is his style. There is no truth in what he says. He is known for making such statements. No SP MP is going anywhere. Sanatan Pandey (Ballia)- SP gave me the opportunity to become an MLA and then an MP. Rajbhar has now made me internationally famous with his comments. SP is not breaking apart. Babu Singh Kushwaha (Jaunpur)- Where is the list he keeps referring to? He should reveal the names of those who are supposedly leaving and explain what they have done wrong. Priya Saroj (Machhlishahr)- I do not wish to comment on someone whose words and actions rarely match. SP defeated him badly in 2024 and will defeat him again in 2027. Every SP MP stands firmly with the leadership. Virendra Singh (Chandauli)- He is trying to prove his usefulness to BJP. When he was with SP, he criticised Yogi Adityanath. Now that he is with BJP, he criticises SP. No one is leaving. Political observers believe Rajbhar's remarks may be aimed at creating a perception of instability within SP. 'Big Split' narrative Rajbhar has repeatedly compared SP's situation to splits witnessed in parties such as Shiv Sena and Trinamool Congress, claiming that a similar development is inevitable in Uttar Pradesh. Such statements may serve as a signal to any disgruntled leaders contemplating a change of allegiance. Interestingly, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav also acknowledged that those driven by fear or personal interest could leave the party, although he maintained confidence in the party's unity. Linking SP leaders to corruption cases Rajbhar has also linked his allegations to investigations into the mining scam and the Gomti Riverfront project. He claims Ram Gopal Yadav is attempting to shield leaders such as Akhilesh Yadav, Shivpal Yadav and Gayatri Prajapati from the consequences of ongoing investigations. Through this narrative, Rajbhar appears to be portraying SP leaders as individuals attempting to protect themselves from legal scrutiny. Other SP MPs also dismiss the claim Akhilesh Yadav (Kannauj)- BJP has broken many parties and persuaded many SP MLAs and MLCs to switch sides in the past. Whoever is driven by fear or self-interest may leave. We need brave people to take on BJP. SP is ready. Iqra Hasan (Kairana)- Rajbhar should examine whether his own MLAs remain with him. I am in SP and will remain in SP. Harendra Malik (Muzaffarnagar)- Rajbhar is trying to return to SP but is not being accepted. He is making such claims only to improve his standing within BJP. Ruchiveera (Moradabad)- He is not a serious politician. He keeps making random statements. In fact, he himself wants to join SP. Devesh Shakya (Etah)- There is no need to attach importance to someone who changes positions constantly. BJP and Rajbhar should focus on managing their own legislators. Mohibullah (Rampur)- SP MPs are united and stand firmly with Akhilesh Yadav. Rajbhar's allegations are completely detached from reality. Aditya Yadav (Badaun)- BJP thrives on conspiracy theories. No SP MP is leaving. Such statements are made simply to attract attention and increase political relevance. Neeraj Maurya (Aonla)- The defeat suffered by Rajbhar's son in 2024 still appears to be troubling him. SP remains united and will perform even better in 2027. Utkarsh Verma 'Madhur' (Kheri)- He speaks without any basis. Rajbhar is nervous because SP is moving towards forming the next government. Anand Bhadauria (Dhaurahra)- There is not an ounce of truth in these allegations. SP leaders cannot compromise with their ideology. Dharmendra Yadav (Azamgarh- My response is the same as that given by Ram Gopal Yadav. Rambhual Nishad (Sultanpur)- SP gave us opportunities and respect. Why would we leave for BJP? Let Rajbhar first demonstrate his own electoral strength. What the Anti-Defection Law says? At least 25 SP MPs would need to defect together Under India's Anti-Defection Law, MPs or MLAs can merge with another party only if at least two-thirds of the legislature party moves together. For SP, which currently has 37 Lok Sabha MPs, at least 25 MPs would have to switch sides collectively. If only 24 or fewer MPs defected, they would lose their Lok Sabha membership and would be required to seek re-election. This makes any large-scale defection significantly more difficult than political rhetoric may suggest. Why BJP wants a larger majority in Parliament The debate over numbers gained significance after the Modi government introduced three Bills in the Lok Sabha between 16 and 18 April 2026. One of these was a Constitutional Amendment Bill aimed at facilitating the implementation of women's reservation before the 2029 elections. The proposal included provisions to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats through amendments to Articles 81 and 82 of the Constitution. Constitutional Amendment fell short A Constitutional Amendment requires a special majority- During voting in April 2026, 528 MPs were present in the Lok Sabha. To secure passage, the Bill required 352 votes. However- As a result, the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill fell short by 54 votes. Political analysts believe this arithmetic explains why BJP is keen to increase its parliamentary strength and secure broader support in the Lok Sabha. However, based on the responses of SP MPs, Rajbhar's prediction of an imminent split currently finds little support within the Samajwadi Party itself.

stories.title: Monsoon stalls near UP border for 5 days:Heatwave alert in 25 districts; Banda remains hottest city in country
stories.summary: The delayed arrival of the monsoon in Uttar Pradesh has led to a fresh surge in temperatures across the state. After reaching the state's border, the monsoon has slowed significantly and has remained stalled near the Uttar Pradesh–Chhattisgarh border for the past five days. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), it could take up to another week for the monsoon to advance and enter Uttar Pradesh. On Friday morning, strong sunshine was reported across most districts. Low wind speeds have increased humidity levels, making conditions more uncomfortable. A rain alert has been issued for 16 districts, while 25 districts remain under a heatwave warning. During the past 24 hours, intense heat has affected large parts of Purvanchal and Bundelkhand. Banda recorded a maximum temperature of 46°C, making it the hottest city in the country. Monsoon progress remains slow The Meteorological Department said weather activity across Uttar Pradesh is currently limited and scattered. While isolated thunderstorms and light drizzle may occur in some areas, these are unlikely to provide any significant relief from the prevailing heat. Forecasters expect temperatures to continue rising over the next five days, with heatwave conditions likely to remain severe during this period. 'No effective weather system Active in UP' Senior meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said that no effective weather system is currently active over Uttar Pradesh. Atul Kumar Singh said- "At present, no effective weather system is active over Uttar Pradesh. As a result, the monsoon's progress remains slow and conditions are not yet favourable for its entry into the state." According to the Meteorological Department, residents may have to wait approximately another week before the monsoon arrives in Uttar Pradesh. Rain alert in 16 districts, heatwave warning in 25 Although a rain alert has been issued for 16 districts, widespread rainfall is not expected immediately. Meanwhile, 25 districts remain under a heatwave alert as temperatures continue to remain well above normal levels. The combination of intense sunshine, low wind speeds and high humidity has increased discomfort across much of the state. 5-day weather forecast for UP 20 June- Most districts across the state are expected to remain cloudy. Heavy rainfall may occur at isolated locations. 21 June- The weather is likely to remain largely clear across Uttar Pradesh. Strong winds are expected, while cloud movement could trigger light drizzle in some areas. 22 June- Cloud cover is expected across most districts. Parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh may experience heavy rainfall accompanied by strong winds. 23 June- Rainfall is likely in both eastern and western Uttar Pradesh. Strong winds may also occur in several areas. 24 June- Most districts are expected to remain under cloudy skies. Heavy rainfall may occur at isolated locations. Heat likely to persist until monsoon advances With the monsoon stalled near the Uttar Pradesh–Chhattisgarh border and no significant weather system currently supporting its advancement, heatwave conditions are expected to continue across much of the state. Meteorologists believe that meaningful relief from the heat is unlikely until the monsoon makes further progress and becomes active over Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Ram Mandir theft row:SIT probe reveals missing gold, silver records; management may shift to administrative officials
stories.summary: The alleged theft of offerings worth crores of rupees at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has sparked a wider debate over the mandir's administrative structure and whether greater government oversight is needed. The controversy has led to discussions about adopting a management model similar to those at major pilgrimage centres such as Shirdi Sai Baba mandir and Vaishno Devi Shrine, where administrative officers play a key role in governance. Sources indicate that the SIT may recommend expanding the role of government-appointed ex officio members within the trust, with the Ayodhya District Magistrate potentially being given a more prominent supervisory role. If accepted, these recommendations could gradually shift greater management responsibility from trustees and priest to administrative officials. The Special Investigation Team (SIT), which has been probing the case for the past four days, found that key administrative functions of the mandir were largely concentrated in the hands of three individuals, Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao. They reportedly oversaw the counting of offerings and their deposit into bank accounts. The investigation has also revealed that ex officio members of the trust, including the Ayodhya District Magistrate, the Additional Chief Secretary (Home) and central government-nominated members, were neither actively involved in decision-making nor regularly informed about the mandir's operations. Investigators have also identified shortcomings in the counting of offerings and security arrangements, findings that are likely to form a key part of the SIT's final report. SIT formed following trust's request On 13 June 2026, the Uttar Pradesh Home Department constituted a three-member SIT following a request from the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. On 15 June, the SIT team, led by Lucknow Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, arrived in Ayodhya and began its investigation from the counting room within the Ram Mandir complex. The team questioned several individuals connected to Mandir operations, including- On 18 June, the fourth day of the investigation, Dr Anil Mishra was questioned for approximately four hours. The SIT subsequently called Tinnu Yadav again for further questioning, interrogating him for around one and a half hours. The team also conducted extensive questioning of employees working in the Mandir basement and reviewed operational procedures with personnel from the bank and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS). In addition, investigators have been recording statements from devotees who donated jewellery, gold and silver ornaments to Ramlala as offerings. Four major irregularities identified The SIT has reportedly uncovered four major areas of concern during its investigation. 1. Offering counting system found lacking transparency Investigators found that the process of removing cash from the 14 donation boxes installed across the Mandir premises, transporting it to the office and subsequently counting it in the designated counting room lacked adequate transparency and security safeguards. According to sources, the system was vulnerable at several stages and did not meet expected standards of accountability. 2. No proper record of gold and silver offerings The SIT reportedly found no comprehensive record of gold and silver jewellery donated by devotees. While cash donation figures were regularly presented during the trust's quarterly meetings, details regarding the quantity and value of precious metal offerings were allegedly not disclosed in a systematic manner. This has raised concerns regarding documentation and inventory management. 3. Recruitment and tender procedures under scrutiny The appointment of security personnel, procurement contracts and recruitment procedures for Mandir employees have also come under suspicion. According to sources, investigators found indications that influential individuals may have played a role in securing jobs for their relatives and associates within the Mandir administration. Tender allocations and procurement decisions are also being examined as part of the probe. 4. Crowd management failures The SIT has reportedly identified shortcomings in multiple aspects of crowd management and visitor services. Areas under scrutiny include- Investigators are examining whether administrative deficiencies contributed to operational failures within the Mandir complex. SIT surprised by influence of Champat Rai's close aide 'Tinnu' According to sources, SIT members were particularly surprised by the influence exercised by Ram Shankar alias Tinnu Yadav within the Ram Janmabhoomi complex. Tinnu Yadav is considered one of the central figures in the investigation and has been questioned extensively by the SIT. Sources suggest that following submission of the investigation report, several employees, including Tinnu Yadav, could face removal from their positions. Legal action may also be recommended against certain individuals, depending on the findings. The investigation has also highlighted concerns regarding security protocols within the Mandir complex. According to sources, while ordinary visitors and even VIP guests are generally prohibited from carrying mobile phones inside the complex, individuals associated with Tinnu Yadav allegedly moved freely without undergoing routine security checks. Sources claim that his guests were accorded treatment comparable to ministerial protocol and were not subjected to the restrictions faced by other visitors. These allegations are being examined as part of the broader inquiry into administrative irregularities. Bank officials point to gaps in the process The SIT also questioned officials from the State Bank of India regarding the counting and deposit of offerings. According to sources, bank officials informed investigators that the contract workers involved in counting donations had been appointed at the recommendation of Trustee Champat Rai. Bank officials reportedly stated that their responsibility begins only when the money reaches them for deposit. They told investigators that they did not know the handling or movement of cash before it arrived at the bank.

stories.title: ₹5 lakh to meet Mayawati, ₹3.35 crore for assembly ticket:BSP UP Chief says, 'Elections are around the corner, full amount must be paid in cash'
stories.summary: ‘When you meet Behanji, carry ₹5 lakh. We will tell her that you want an Assembly ticket. There will be no accounting for those ₹5 lakh. For the ticket, you will have to pay ₹3.35 crore. Deposit ₹1 crore to ₹1.5 crore now, and you will get one to one-and-a-half months for the remaining amount. If the government is formed, we guarantee that you will be made a minister.’ These claims were made by Vishwanath Pal, Uttar Pradesh President of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), during conversations with a Bhaskar reporter posing as a prospective Assembly candidate. To investigate the process of obtaining a ticket from the BSP — a party recognised as a national political organisation — a Bhaskar reporter prepared a profile portraying himself as an aspiring politician. He established contacts with BSP leaders and workers before expressing interest in contesting from Lucknow's Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) Assembly constituency. The first contact was with Shailendra Gautam, BSP's Lucknow district president. Meeting the BSP District President The reporter met Shailendra Gautam at Shailendra Traders near Raghuvar Marriage Hall in Indiranagar, Lucknow. During a conversation in a closed room, Gautam allegedly explained the process for meeting BSP chief Mayawati and discussed the cost of obtaining a party ticket. Reporter: Now tell me, how will I meet Behanji? What do I need to do? Shailendra Gautam: To meet Behanji as a candidate, you will have to bring ₹5 lakh. You will be introduced to Behanji as a claimant from BKT. Behanji herself will speak to you. You will be given an empty envelope there. You will put the money in the envelope and place it on Behanji's table with your own hands. For this seat, Behanji has mentioned one Pandit candidate and one Thakur candidate. The Thakur candidate is already active and moving around in the constituency. Reporter: So, after bringing ₹5 lakh, what happens next? Shailendra Gautam: The ₹5 lakh is only for the meeting. There will be no accounting for it. In a way, it is a gift to Behanji. After that, Behanji's office will tell you the amount that must be deposited for the ticket. You will get one to one-and-a-half months for this. Once the amount is deposited, your candidature will be announced before a crowd of 10,000–15,000 people. After that, you will begin working in the constituency. 'Every seat has a different rate' The reporter then sought details about the amount allegedly required to secure a BSP ticket. Shailendra Gautam: You will have to deposit ₹3.35 crore. Reporter: You mean the remaining ₹3 crore has to be paid later? Shailendra Gautam: No, the total amount is ₹3.35 crore. You will first take ₹5 lakh and meet Behanji. You will receive her blessings. She will tell you to begin preparations. The amount can be deposited either in one instalment or over one to one-and-a-half months. Sometimes people deposit ₹20 lakh, sometimes ₹50 lakh. Those amounts are properly recorded in the register. But the full ₹3.35 crore must be deposited within the stipulated time. Reporter: Suppose I pay in instalments and another person deposits the entire amount before I complete payment. Will my ticket be cancelled? Shailendra Gautam: No, that will not happen. We will manage it. Some flexibility is always possible. Behanji takes care of those who deposit first. 'Many leaders have grown through BSP' Shailendra Gautam: That is why Bhai Umashankar Singh is a star in Behanji's eyes. Whenever the time comes, he delivers. That is why Behanji respects him. Reporter: He is a very influential person. Shailendra Gautam: He was not influential earlier. BSP made him influential. Many such people in the BSP immediately deposit money when asked. Madhogarh's ticket in the Chitrakoot division has already been finalised. The candidate is a Brahmin. The ticket was announced first and he is already campaigning. Barabanki Sadar's ticket has also been finalised. Around 20 to 25 tickets have already been decided. Reporter: Does even a difficult seat cost ₹3.35 crore? Shailendra Gautam: No. Not every seat. Take Lucknow East, for example. The party knows it is a difficult constituency, but we still have to field a candidate. If someone wants to become a leader, let them contest. If the government is formed, Behanji will reward them in some way. The reporter also asked whether Mayawati considered a candidate's political experience. Reporter: Will Behanji not examine my background, considering that I have never been involved in politics? Shailendra Gautam: No. She will only seek information about any cases against you. Just tell her, "Behanji, I was previously involved in business and now I want to serve society by joining the party." Reporter: I would like to meet Behanji through you. Shailendra Gautam: We are organisational people. If someone contributes willingly, that is a different matter. Reporter: Suppose I pay ₹2 crore in cash and ₹1 crore in gold. Will that work? Shailendra Gautam: No. The entire amount must be in cash. I have served as district president for four years and as Lucknow divisional in-charge. Behanji trusts me a great deal. State President quotes the same amount To verify the claims, the reporter approached Uttar Pradesh BSP President Vishwanath Pal. Pal invited the reporter to his private office on the second floor of Shaligram Apartment near 1090 Chauraha in Lucknow. The reporter met him twice. The first meeting was introductory. During the second meeting, another reporter accompanied him while posing as a financier. According to the account, Vishwanath Pal quoted the same figures and outlined the same process as described by the district president. 'Deposit ₹1 crore first' Vishwanath Pal: Suppose ₹1 crore is deposited and no other claimant emerges. We discussed ₹3.35 crore with you. If you later say you cannot pay more and still want to contest, then the party may decide accordingly. Contesting itself requires expenditure. That is why we told you that after paying the ₹5 lakh, you must proceed further. The ₹3.35 crore will be recorded in writing. In some situations, the amount may even be reduced, but that generally happens only if we delay announcing the candidate. Reporter: But that carries a risk. Vishwanath Pal: Exactly. Suppose Behanji becomes angry. There is currently a claimant who gave ₹5 lakh and kept promising to arrange the rest. One day he invited me for tea and showed me ₹1.5 crore in a bag. He said he would arrange another ₹1 crore and deposit ₹2.5 crore. He told me this on 15 April. Since then, he has not answered calls. He was supposed to bring ₹2 crore today. We told him not to come because Behanji had become displeased. We instructed him to collect the full amount before approaching us again. This is regarding the Barabanki Sadar Assembly seat. Reporter: How much time will I get? Vishwanath Pal: As little as possible. If you return after 10 days and someone else has completed the process, your opportunity may be gone. If you decide now, your meeting with Behanji can be scheduled immediately. Reporter: What benefit will I get if I join the BSP? Vishwanath Pal: If the government is formed, I guarantee that I will make you a minister. This is a good seat for us. Nakul Dubey won from here and became a minister. Reporter: After giving ₹5 lakh, how much time will I get? Vishwanath Pal: Paying ₹5 lakh alone means nothing. You should immediately arrange at least ₹1 crore to ₹1.5 crore. You will then get roughly one month to arrange the remainder. Elections are very close. The election announcement could come at any time. Behanji has already called a meeting on the 24th. The reporter then asked whether a person who merely wanted to meet Mayawati and seek blessings would also have to pay. Vishwanath Pal: Azamgarh, Jaunpur and Shahganj have already been announced. Madhogarh has also been announced. One Thakur candidate has been declared. Five candidates have been announced so far. Discussions are continuing for the remaining seats. Only those seats where money has arrived have been announced. Reporter: If this person accompanying me also wants to meet Behanji and seek blessings, will he have to pay another ₹5 lakh? Vishwanath Pal: No. We can arrange a joint meeting. Otherwise, meeting Behanji separately costs ₹2 lakh. Reporter: Whatever remains, we will contribute separately to your service. Vishwanath Pal: We will tell Behanji that these people want to contest and that these are their associates. We will arrange a private meeting. Winning an Assembly election gives a person considerable influence and opportunities. We would like you to bring more than ₹5 lakh on the day of the meeting. Reporter: When can you take me? Vishwanath Pal: Whenever you say. If you want to go now, I can call and arrange it immediately. Reporter: Apart from ₹5 lakh, how much should I bring initially? Vishwanath Pal: Whatever you can arrange. Ultimately, ₹3.35 crore is required. Bring as much as possible because there is very little time. Why did the sting not go further ? The day after the meeting, Vishwanath Pal allegedly informed the reporter that an appointment with Mayawati had been secured. However, the operation was not taken any further. According to the report, security arrangements and checks before meeting the BSP supremo are extremely strict, making it difficult to carry concealed recording equipment. As a result, no further sting operation was conducted. Indications about BSP's Election strategy During the conversations, party leaders also gave indications regarding preparations for the upcoming Assembly elections- About the BSP Founded by Kanshi Ram on 14 April 1984 Kanshi Ram founded the Bahujan Samaj Party on 14 April 1984, the birth anniversary of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar. The party's election symbol is the elephant. Former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati currently serves as the party's national president and has held the office of Chief Minister four times. The BSP advocates for the rights and political representation of Bahujan communities, Dalits, backward classes and other marginalised sections of society. BSP's vote share In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BSP secured 12.9% of the vote and won just one seat. However, it remained the state's third-largest party in terms of vote share. The party's vote share in recent Assembly elections was- 2007: 30% 2012: 26% 2017: 22% 2022: 12.9% The figures indicate a steady decline in electoral support over the past four Assembly elections, despite the party retaining a significant presence across Uttar Pradesh.

Critics argue this tactic endangered lives in a state already battling a severe opioid crisis. The DEA defends its actions, stating investigations were court-authorized and aimed at dismantling major criminal organizations, asserting that targeting kingpins ultimately saves more lives.

stories.title: These mountains in Albania kept this giant underground lake hidden for centuries; now it's the world's largest underground thermal lake
'Operation Tiger continues all 365 days': Shinde faction set to induct six rebel MPs from Uddhav camp
stories.summary: Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs are officially joining the Eknath Shinde-led faction today, significantly boosting the ruling party's strength in the Lok Sabha. This move marks a major blow to Uddhav Thackeray's party, with the rebels citing ideological differences and proximity to Congress as reasons for their departure. The split intensifies political turmoil, as the Shinde camp welcomes the MPs, continuing its 'Operation Tiger'.

stories.title: 'Operation Keechad': Congress targets BJP after Shinde camp triggers new Uddhav Sena crisis
stories.summary: Congress leader Pawan Khera has strongly criticized the BJP, dubbing the recent defection of Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs to Eknath Shinde's faction as "Operation Keechad." He questioned the BJP's motives behind allegedly "stealing" MPs from opposition parties, suggesting it could be an attempt to alter the constitution. This move follows a similar setback for the Trinamool Congress in West Bengal, where several MPs also shifted allegiance.

stories.title: 10 longest bridges in the US: From the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway to the Seven Mile Bridge
'Your loyalty is for sale': Aaditya Thackeray hits out at 'greedy MPs' as Uddhav Sena battles fresh rebellion
stories.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray has strongly criticized six Lok Sabha MPs who are reportedly shifting allegiance to the Eknath Shinde faction. Thackeray accused them of betraying voters' mandate and selling their loyalty for political gain, calling their actions a 'shocking example of dirty politics.' The move deepens the internal crisis for Uddhav Thackeray's party, with disciplinary action anticipated against the absent MPs.

stories.title: School shooting in central Philippines leaves three dead, five injured
stories.summary: A shooting at a school in central Philippines on Monday left three individuals dead. Authorities quickly arrested one suspect, who is a minor, while they continue their search for another assailant. The gunfire injured eight people, leaving five hospitalized. The police are diligently investigating the motives behind this tragic event as they attempt to locate the remaining suspect.

stories.title: 'Ain't getting bit by that, bro': Huge uproar after Los Angeles police kill pet dog minutes after family celebrates NBA Knicks win - video
stories.summary: Outrage erupted after LAPD released body-camera footage showing officers fatally shooting Jameson, a two-year-old dog, during a disturbance call. Police believed the noise was a woman screaming, but it was a family celebrating the Knicks' NBA championship. The dog, wearing a Knicks jersey, was shot after exiting the apartment. The incident has sparked protests and calls for accountability, with the Mayor ordering a thorough investigation.

stories.title: Drone scare over Moscow: Four airports shut, nearly 60 UAVs shot down
stories.summary: Moscow's airspace faced disruption as air defence systems intercepted 59 drones targeting the capital, leading to a temporary shutdown of all four airports. This incident highlights ongoing cross-border attacks, with Russia having previously struck Ukraine's Odesa region with a ballistic missile, causing casualties and damage to an agricultural facility. The situation underscores the escalating tensions and the persistent threat of aerial assaults.

stories.title: China retaliates against US blacklist, targets defence and rare earth firms with export controls
stories.summary: China has retaliated against US export controls by imposing its own restrictions on 10 American defense and rare earth companies. Additionally, Beijing has banned government procurement of products from 46 US firms, including major defense contractors like Lockheed Martin and Raytheon. This move escalates economic tensions following the US expansion of its blacklist targeting Chinese military-linked entities, signaling a broader strategic rivalry.

stories.title: 'Restore water supply immediately': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke appeals as protesters spend second night at Jantar Mantar
stories.summary: Protesters at Jantar Mantar, led by Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke, are demanding the restoration of water supply and better facilities amidst their sit-in over the NEET-UG paper leak. Dipke also criticized police for questioning those donating supplies. The group, seeking compensation and the Education Minister's resignation, vows to continue their protest until their demands are met, highlighting widespread public support for the cause.

No JEE ranks, GATE scores in resumes, IIT students told

Congress vs Congress again: A day after backlash for PM Modi praise, Shashi Tharoor faces criticism over Kashmir remarks
stories.summary: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor faced internal party criticism for his remarks on Kashmir's progress towards normalcy and for praising PM Modi's stance on civilian sailors' safety. Critics questioned his engagement with party members and ground realities in Kashmir, while another party leader sarcastically questioned his interpretation of Modi's statements. Tharoor defended his comments, citing widely published reports and emphasizing concern for Indian lives.

stories.title: Spanish proverb of the day: 'A bird in hand is worth more than a hundred flying around'
stories.summary: A classic Spanish saying, 'A bird in the hand is worth more than a hundred flying,' highlights the importance of appreciating what you have rather than chasing uncertain prospects. This proverb serves as a universal reminder that we often prioritize security over risk, a concept supported by behavioral economics. It's a vital lesson for making sound choices in finance, career paths, and everyday life.

stories.title: SRS 2024: 3.5% people were 'widowed, divorced or separated' with 5.5% women and 1.6% men
stories.summary: Latest data reveals a significant gender disparity in marital status, with 3.5% of the population widowed, divorced, or separated in 2024. Women disproportionately represent this group at 5.4% compared to men's 1.6%, highlighting unique challenges. Southern states, particularly Tamil Nadu, show the highest percentages for both the general population and women in this category.

stories.title: Heat dome over Europe brings travel chaos, health alerts and wildlife stress
stories.summary: Europe is grappling with a severe heatwave, with temperatures soaring towards 40°C, triggering health alerts and transport chaos. Italy has issued red alerts for eight cities, while France faces significant rail disruptions. Wildlife is also under immense pressure. Experts link these extreme conditions to climate change, with concerns growing over prolonged heat and its impact on public safety and infrastructure across the continent.

stories.title: Portuguese proverb of the day: 'One day belongs to the prey, another to the hunter'
stories.summary: The age-old Portuguese saying, "One day belongs to the prey, another to the hunter," encapsulates the unpredictable nature of life. This proverb serves as a poignant reminder that success and failure are fleeting. It calls for humility in triumph and instills hope in defeat, demonstrating that today's champions can easily falter tomorrow, whether in sports, business, or personal endeavors.

stories.title: Annamalai seeks thorough probe into ammonia gas leak that claimed seven lives
stories.summary: A tragic incident at a prawn farm in Tiruvallur district has resulted in the loss of seven lives due to an ammonia gas leak, leaving many workers gasping for air. K Annamalai, the former BJP Tamil Nadu president, has demanded a comprehensive investigation and accountability for any negligence. In response, the state government has initiated a three-member committee to examine the circumstances, with updates anticipated shortly.

stories.title: NY boy finds mom’s dead body with throat slit; ‘someone followed her home,’ says husband
'Processed through robust system': CBSE declares over 87% revaluation results as marking controversy persists
stories.summary: The CBSE has begun releasing Class 12 verification and re-evaluation results, covering over 87% of applications. This follows student concerns about potential answer sheet mismatches with their handwriting, raising transparency issues. The board assures a robust system and urges students to rely on official communications, with remaining results to be announced soon via DigiLocker.

stories.title: How China is using maritime tactics and propaganda to squeeze Taiwan
stories.summary: Taiwan's security official warns China is increasingly using 'grey-zone' tactics like coast guard patrols and legal claims to pressure the island, moving away from direct military threats. Beijing is exploiting international law and maritime activities to advance its objectives, while Taiwan is urged to adopt 'absolute transparency' and enhance regional cooperation to counter these evolving challenges amidst ongoing Chinese military drills.

stories.title: ‘No leak related complaints received’: NTA DG says NEET-UG 2026 re-exam conducted smoothly
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has announced that the NEET-UG 2026 re-examination took place without any issues across the country, ensuring tight security measures were in place. There were no reports of paper leaks, boosting officials' confidence in the examination's integrity. With over 2 million students participating, results are expected to be released earlier than initially thought, following the cancellation of the May 3rd exam over leak suspicions.

stories.title: Abhishek meets Birla, wants 20 TMC rebels disqualified
stories.summary: On rebel MPs statement they have the requisite twothird numbers — threshold required to be exempt from the law and retain membership of the House — he said that “the merger will be accepted only when two-third of the political party merges with another political party and not just legislative party”.

stories.title: Former USSR leader's great-grandson captured by Ukraine: Reports
stories.summary: Reports indicate Anton Milaev, adopted great-grandson of Leonid Brezhnev, has been captured by Ukrainian forces. Milaev, reportedly a sapper, was last heard from in November 2025. Ukrainian military intelligence and prisoner of war coordination sources have allegedly confirmed his custody in the Kherson region. His presence on a Ukrainian 'enemies' database has also been noted. The circumstances of his capture and potential for exchange remain unclear amidst ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Napoleon Bonaparte: "The only victories which leave no regret are…" - the surprising belief of history's most famous conqueror
'Keir Starmer will resign': Donald Trump makes bold claim, accuses UK PM of 'failing badly' on 2 subjects
'There is only one Shiv Sena, and it is led by me': Uddhav Thackeray hits back at Amit Shah
stories.summary: Uddhav Thackeray has declared his faction as the sole Shiv Sena, countering Union home minister Amit Shah's statement. Thackeray accused the BJP of attempting to dismantle his party and poach its leaders, contrasting this with the Congress, with whom his party fought for decades but was never targeted for destruction. This comes after the Election Commission recognized Eknath Shinde's group as the official Shiv Sena.

stories.title: Telangana Congress calls for 'transparency' in SIR, meets state poll chief

'Centre has put us in danger': Karnataka CM urges Congress cadre to act as voter help desks amid SIR
'An Indian and a Pakistani': JD Vance names two 'very important' people in his life
Nihangs storm Uttarakhand Gurdwara, hold manager hostage over arrests after Karnaprayag clash
stories.summary: Nihangs have taken a gurdwara manager hostage in Uttarakhand's Rudraprayag, demanding the release of four members arrested after a clash in Karnaprayag. The group, armed with traditional weapons, occupied the gurdwara roof, raising slogans. The incident stems from a dispute over parking that escalated into violence, leading to the arrests. Authorities are negotiating for their descent while investigating the initial clash.

stories.title: SIT directs Ram Temple trust officials not to leave Ayodhya as donation probe continues
stories.summary: The investigation into alleged embezzlement of Ram Temple funds has escalated, leading a Special Investigation Team to restrict trust and temple officials from exiting Ayodhya. As discrepancies surface, investigators are meticulously analyzing donation records, which include valuable items. They are also reviewing large transactions from the Maha Kumbh festival, when considerable contributions were made, along with examining land acquisitions and material procurement associated with the temple project.

stories.title: 'Modi destroying India, Trump the world': Kharge takes 'good friends' dig at PM
stories.summary: Blaming Trump for rising fuel prices, he criticised the Modi government's foreign policy, saying India had moved away from its long-standing non-aligned approach. "India followed a policy of non-alignment since Nehru's time and maintained good relations with all countries. But that policy has been abandoned, and Modi, by going around calling everyone his friend and hugging them, has brought us to this situation."

stories.title: Quote of the day by Benjamin Graham: "But investing isn't about beating others at their game. It's about…" - the timeless wisdom of the man who taught Warren Buffett
'We are not Indians': Canadian woman rants about FIFA opening ceremony performance
NEET-UG re-exam 2026: Tight security, dress code debates and reactions to 'tough' paper — how the day unfolded
stories.summary: Millions of medical aspirants reappeared for the NEET-UG 2026 re-exam nationwide after the original test was cancelled due to paper leak allegations. Unprecedented security measures, including biometrics and CCTV, were implemented. While students reported a moderate-to-tough paper, particularly Physics, the day also saw emotional moments and entry disputes. The focus now shifts to answer keys, results, and the ongoing CBI investigation.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: NEET-UG re-exam concludes for 22 lakh candidates; ammonia gas leak kills 7 workers in Tamil Nadu & more
Green Party leader Zack Polanski blames Elon Musk, politicians for anti-Muslim attacks in Edinburgh; 5 injured
Ten years after Brexit vote, Britain is still wrestling with the fallout
stories.summary: A decade after the UK's Brexit vote, the nation grapples with its economic and social fallout. Despite promises of renewed prosperity, businesses face trade hurdles with the EU, and economists estimate a significant economic contraction. While immigration from EU nations has decreased, overall net migration has fallen, yet illegal crossings remain a politically charged issue.

stories.title: Indian woman facing deportation granted residency after husband's previous sponsorship of two ex-partners
Uddhav camp MP confirms crossover to ruling Sena: ‘Fund crunch for constituency, caustic remarks’
stories.summary: A Shiv Sena (UBT) Lok Sabha MP, Nagesh Patil Ashtikar, has switched to the Eknath Shinde faction, citing a need for development funds for his constituency. He stated that the limited MPLADS fund was insufficient to address public expectations. Ashtikar also alluded to "certain remarks" made by a senior Sena (UBT) leader as a catalyst for his decision, suggesting a lack of respect within the party.

stories.title: 'Yoga is science for inner well-being': Sadhguru; over 50,000 take part in Isha Foundation yoga sessions held across India
‘Truth must come out’: Karnataka BJP to ask MLAs to swear before Lord Manjunatha in cross-voting probe
stories.summary: Karnataka BJP is investigating alleged cross-voting by its MLAs in the recent Legislative Council polls, which saw the ruling Congress secure a significant victory. Party president B Y Vijayendra announced a legislature party meeting at Dharmasthala, where MLAs might take an oath before Lord Manjunatha to reveal the truth. He termed the alleged betrayal a serious matter that will be pursued to its conclusion, aiming to restore party worker confidence.

stories.title: 'Big names involved, govt may fall': Arvind Kejriwal questions lack of CBI, ED action in Ram Temple donation 'theft' case
stories.summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has alleged that "big names" are involved in the Ram Temple donation theft case, claiming the government could face collapse if their identities are revealed. He questioned the lack of FIRs despite reports of crores in cash and valuables being stolen, urging swift action to protect public faith over political interests.

stories.title: How El Nino could affect India's monsoon and your household budget - explained
Why Starmer is facing fresh pressure to exit after Labour rival Andy Burnham’s victory
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces intense pressure following Andy Burnham's return to Parliament, sparking leadership challenge speculation. Despite denials from senior ministers, Starmer is reportedly reflecting on his position amid Labour's recent electoral setbacks and declining approval. Burnham has signaled his ambition, warning the party needs a "final chance to change." Starmer, however, vows to contest any leadership bid, insisting he will not step aside voluntarily.

stories.title: From mountains to plains to high seas, Indian forces take part in yoga sessions pan-India; Rajnath performs yoga with 1,000 soldiers in Shillong, calls it ‘holistic science’
stories.summary: Across India and its waters, armed forces personnel marked the 12th International Day of Yoga with widespread sessions. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh led a large gathering in Shillong, emphasizing yoga's role in holistic well-being and a disciplined life. From high-altitude posts to parade grounds, soldiers, sailors, and air warriors embraced the theme 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing,' showcasing India's ancient traditions as a global movement for humanity's health.

stories.title: Grooming gang row: British MP Rupert Lowe hits back at political opponents for trying to 'demonise' him
Modi commissions 3 indigenous frontline naval ships, says ‘strong maritime capability deciding factor for country's eco, strategic influence’
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi commissioned three indigenous naval platforms—INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak, and INS Agray—in Kolkata, marking a significant stride in India's self-reliance in defence manufacturing. These advanced vessels bolster the nation's maritime security and operational capabilities. The event underscores India's growing prowess in shipbuilding and its commitment to becoming a major global defence producer, with over 40 indigenously built warships inducted recently.

stories.title: Father's Day 2026: UAE leaders pay emotional tributes to fathers, say 'we are what they built'
Why Bürgenstock? Inside the Qatari-owned Swiss resort hosting US-Iran talks
Sumit Roy, key aide of TMC's Abhishek Banerjee, booked in fraud and forgery case
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee's close aide, Sumit Roy, faces fraud and forgery charges in West Bengal. Roy, who is currently absconding, has also been implicated in a separate land-grab case, leading to a lookout notice and searches at Banerjee's residence. The developments follow the party's recent electoral setback in the state where it lost power after 15 years.

stories.title: Why ecologists are concerned about the Great Nicobar Project
PM Modi delays heading home from Delhi airport to ensure smooth commute for NEET-UG re-exam candidates
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi delayed his departure from Delhi airport on Sunday to prevent traffic disruptions for students appearing for the NEET-UG re-exam. Arriving at 1:15 pm, he waited to ensure smooth passage to examination centres across 551 cities and 14 international locations. The exam, held at 5,440 centres, featured extensive CCTV surveillance and jammers to prevent malpractice, with heightened security and strict checks in Delhi.

stories.title: 'The moment we ... ' : Pakistan defence minister issues war threat to India over Indus Water Treaty
'Amit Shah insulted Sena (UBT)': Sanjay Raut on 'only one Shiv Sena' remark
NEET aspirant given Abu Dhabi centre takes re-test in Nagpur after NTA correction
stories.summary: A NEET-UG 2026 candidate from Nagpur, initially assigned an exam center in Abu Dhabi, successfully appeared for the re-test in his hometown after the NTA revised the location. The issue gained national attention, prompting swift action from the agency. While the NTA stated the city change was made via the candidate's login, the family maintained their preference for local centers. This incident occurred amidst the ongoing NEET-UG 2026 re-examination.

'It connects everyone': PM Modi leads Yoga Day celebrations from Kolkata's Red Road — in pictures
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi championed yoga as a unifying force during International Yoga Day celebrations in Kolkata. He emphasized its role in promoting physical, mental, and emotional well-being for all ages, particularly highlighting 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing.' The Prime Minister urged making yoga a way of life, not just an annual event, and thanked Kolkata for its hospitality and cleanliness efforts.

Pradhan assures smooth NEET retest, targets Rahul over ‘irresponsible’ conduct

Cockroach Janta Party overnight protest: Abhijeet Dipke claims authorities cut off water, electricity at Jantar Mantar
stories.summary: Protesters at Jantar Mantar, demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over examination controversies, face water supply issues in restrooms. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) highlighted the lack of basic facilities for demonstrators, contrasting it with the minister's situation. Meanwhile, the NEET-UG 2026 re-examination is underway nationwide, with CJP inviting aspirants to join their protest post-exam.

stories.title: Can yoga help age better? Why healthy ageing is the theme of Yoga Day 2026
New book reveals Trump compared himself to Mao, Stalin, Attila the Hun, called Netanyahu a 'con man'
'We are all grateful to PM Modi': Top ministers, CMs perform yoga across India
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi led International Yoga Day celebrations in Kolkata, emphasizing "Yoga for Healthy Ageing" and its role in maintaining physical and mental well-being. Across India, Union ministers and chief ministers participated in mass yoga sessions, highlighting yoga's global reach and its contribution to a healthier, more vibrant nation. The day marked a collective global celebration of yoga's benefits.

stories.title: 'More flexible at 40, energetic at 50': PM Modi on healthy ageing, yoga's benefits - top quotes
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to integrate yoga into their daily lives, not just observe it on a single day, during International Yoga Day celebrations in Kolkata. He emphasized yoga's role as a global movement fostering physical health, mental well-being, and emotional resilience for all ages, particularly highlighting 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing'.

stories.title: Prohibition hits European summer: France bans booze at music festival as heatwave hits 41°C
'250-ft gash, poured chemicals': Trump claims vandals damaged Reflecting Pool
FSSAI turns lens on 'natural', 'healthy' labels
stories.summary: India's food regulator, FSSAI, is cracking down on misleading health claims on food and supplement labels. Products marketed as "natural," "healthy," or "no added sugar" are under scrutiny for potentially deceiving consumers. This intensified enforcement follows rising complaints and social media attention, aiming to ensure transparency and protect public health by urging consumers to look beyond catchy marketing phrases.

stories.title: At Lahore's 'Eton', Pakistani alum pays tribute to Indian dost
stories.summary: A classroom at Lahore's Aitchison College, once attended by leaders from undivided Punjab, now bridges India and Pakistan. A tribute to former Punjab CM Harcharan Singh Brar, funded by his 100-year-old schoolmate Syed Babar Ali, highlights enduring friendships forged before Partition. This initiative is part of a larger effort to remember the institution's pre-1947 past, honouring students and teachers scattered by history.

stories.title: Rs 28 LPA in Bengaluru or $60K per year in US: Indian student on F-1 visa asks which one is wiser to choose
Digital marking: CBSE to consult stakeholders
stories.summary: CBSE's on-screen marking system for Class XII exams faces an uncertain future. The board will consult students, teachers, and parents before deciding on its continuation for 2027 and potential expansion to Class X. This review follows complaints about the system's debut, including scanning issues and unevaluated answers, and aims to address gaps exposed during recent exams and rebuild trust.

stories.title: UK detains Indian captain of sanctioned ship, family in Uttarakhand pleads for release
stories.summary: An Indian captain, Ajay Pant, has been arrested in the UK and charged with breaching sanctions after his Russian oil tanker was intercepted in the English Channel. The vessel, en route to India, was found to be stateless. Pant's family in Uttarakhand has appealed to the Indian government for his safe return, while authorities are coordinating efforts for his release.

stories.title: Maximum in a day: Three Indian-flagged ships safely cross Strait of Hormuz
Shashi Tharoor's praise for PM Modi sparks political slugfest
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor's assertion that Prime Minister Modi raised concerns about Indian civilian sailors with US President Trump has sparked internal party friction. This statement contradicts Rahul Gandhi's claim that the issue was ignored. The BJP has seized on Tharoor's remarks, highlighting the divergence within Congress and his praise for the Prime Minister's leadership.

stories.title: 'Can I survive with Rs 6 crore in India without a job?' Indian man on Green Card queue gets laid off
Cocaine hidden inside cheese powder box: Indian man arrested on US-Canada border, says he didn't know about the drug
Ladakh groups accuse Centre of reneging on agreement, call shutdown
stories.summary: Ladakh's political groups, Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, have called for a shutdown on June 23, accusing the Centre of reneging on agreements regarding legislative powers and constitutional safeguards. They warn of renewed agitation if their demands for full statehood and Sixth Schedule status are not met, emphasizing that public mobilization will proceed despite the Dalai Lama's upcoming visit.

stories.title: Kheer Bhawani yatra begins; 8,500 pilgrims in 214 buses leave Jammu
stories.summary: Over 8,500 pilgrims, predominantly Kashmiri Pandits, embarked on their journey from Jammu for the annual Kheer Bhawani Mela. The significant increase in registrations this year is attributed to a peaceful environment, enhanced security, and comprehensive arrangements. Officials have been stationed at various shrines across Kashmir to ensure smooth proceedings for the devotees participating in the revered yatra.

stories.title: Jammu & Kashmir suspends cardiologist over ‘false’ Ayushman-Bharat claims
'On his way back': Sena (UBT) hopeful rebel MP Nimbalkar may not defect
stories.summary: Nimbalkar was among the six MPs who stayed away from the June 17 meeting convened by the Uddhav Thackeray-led party. With Shiv Sena (UBT) holding nine seats in the Lok Sabha, the rebel faction requires the support of at least six MPs, or two-thirds of the parliamentary party, to avoid attracting provisions of the anti-defection law.

stories.title: With eyes on 2027 polls, BJP chief Nitin Nabin begins Punjab tour
stories.summary: BJP chief Nitin Nabin launched a three-day Punjab visit, emphasizing a vision for the state mirroring Maharaja Ranjit Singh's era. His tour, including prayers at the Golden Temple and a Jalandhar roadshow, signals intensified preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. Nabin met with the Punjab BJP core committee to strategize on organizational strengthening and booth-level expansion, aiming to form a 'double-engine government' under PM Modi's leadership.

stories.title: IAF sorties, AI-monitored CCTV feeds and more: Inside NEET-UG re-exam preparations across India
stories.summary: Authorities have implemented extensive security measures for the NEET re-exam on June 21, including a ban on Telegram and Indian Air Force involvement in transporting question papers. Over 13,500 CCTV cameras, 51,000 jammers, and AI surveillance are in place. Massive police and paramilitary forces are deployed, with stringent biometric verification and mock drills conducted to ensure a fair and secure examination process nationwide.

'Extreme alert': Suspected cyberattack prompts Brazil to shut down emergency alert network
stories.summary: Brazil's emergency alert system was temporarily shut down after a suspected cyberattack flooded the nation with false "Extreme Alert" messages overnight. Residents were jolted awake by the disruptive notifications, which authorities believe were remotely activated by an intruder. The Civil Defense agency is now working with the Federal Police to investigate the hack and will restore the system only after enhancing security measures.

stories.title: Pak court jails 4 Imran Khan party leaders for 10 years, acquits ex-FM
Ajit Doval to host BRICS security conclave: Cross-border terrorism, Middle East conflict in focus; China FM among key attendees
stories.summary: India hosts a crucial BRICS security conclave in New Delhi, bringing together top officials including China's Wang Yi and Russia's Shoigu. Discussions will centre on global flashpoints like the Middle East conflict and the Ukraine war, alongside regional security and terrorism concerns. This meeting serves as a vital prelude to the upcoming BRICS Summit, with a focus on non-traditional security challenges and emerging technologies.

stories.title: African proverb of the day: 'Don't let your mouth carry you where your foot can't bring you back from' because words travel farther than we can
SOP released to conserve sea turtles across 36 islands of Lakshadweep
stories.summary: A new Standard Operating Procedure has been launched for sea turtle conservation in Lakshadweep, offering a unified framework for management and monitoring. This initiative aims to protect all four major sea turtle species, which are legally protected. The SOP addresses nesting site security, migration tracking, and rescue protocols, building on the success of a decade-long ban on poaching that has boosted green turtle populations in the region.

stories.title: What is driving the latest wave of protests in PoK — and what it means for Pakistan
stories.summary: The situation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) has come to light, exposing serious governance challenges that undermine Pakistan's portrayal as a peace broker in the region. Protests began with economic discontent over rising electricity costs and inflation, swiftly evolving into calls for political reforms that would eliminate reserved seats for refugees in the PoK assembly.

stories.title: 'Heard what PM Modi didn't say': Congress taunts Shashi Tharoor; he claps back with 'I read widely'
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor defended his remarks praising PM Modi's handling of the civilian sailors' issue, stating he relied on widely published reports. This followed criticism from colleague Pawan Khera, who questioned Tharoor's claims, citing a lack of mention in official statements. The BJP also weighed in, highlighting perceived internal Congress divisions over the matter.

stories.summary: India, once concerned about a population boom, now faces a declining birth rate, with the Total Fertility Rate dropping to 1.9 children per woman, below the replacement level. This significant shift reflects women's increased educational attainment, career focus, and later marriages, leading to more personal choices about family planning. The narrative is evolving from population control to individual decisions, marking a societal transition.

Maharashtra's Deputy Chief Minister confirmed the appeal to the Bombay High Court, citing disappointment with the special court's decision. The acquittal, nearly two decades after the murders, hinged on the unreliability of a key witness. This high-profile political murder case is set for further legal battle.

Iran-US peace deal under threat? Israel launches strikes at Lebanon despite ceasefire, killing 5
stories.summary: A fragile ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah shattered Saturday as fresh Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon reportedly killed five, including a soldier and two children. This escalation, less than 24 hours after a US-Qatar brokered truce, raises serious doubts about the broader Iran-US peace framework. Both sides accuse each other of violations, with Israel vowing to continue operations to protect its civilians, while Hezbollah insists on defending its land.

The BJP has strongly condemned the act, accusing the Congress of disrespecting Hindu faith and using religious symbols for political gain. Congress leaders, however, defended the gesture, questioning the BJP's monopoly on religious figures and asserting Gandhi's distinct identity.

stories.title: PM Modi wishes President Murmu on birthday, joins her in Odisha to launch projects worth over Rs 47,600 crore
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated President Droupadi Murmu's birthday by highlighting her dedication to public service before joining her in Odisha. Their visit included engagements in her native Mayurbhanj district and the inauguration of development projects exceeding Rs 47,600 crore. These initiatives span energy, infrastructure, healthcare, and more, aiming to boost connectivity and create jobs across the state.

Raut also drew parallels with West Bengal's Suvendu Adhikari, suggesting both leaders make provocative statements while in power. He warned that public backlash awaits them once their power diminishes, amidst speculation of MPs switching parties.

stories.title: Bolivia crisis explained: State of emergency declared after 50 days of protests
stories.summary: Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz has declared a state of emergency after nearly 50 days of crippling protests over economic hardship. Demonstrations, fueled by anger over rising costs and subsidy cuts, are demanding the president's resignation, despite recent government concessions.

stories.summary: Afghanistan's Taliban government claims its forces conducted airstrikes on militant hideouts in Pakistan's Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces. Islamabad vehemently denies this, stating only a drone entered its airspace and was intercepted. This latest exchange escalates tensions, with both nations blaming each other for cross-border militancy and recent deadly incidents, despite Chinese mediation efforts.

stories.summary: Political tensions escalate between Shiv Sena factions as Sanjay Raut fires back at Eknath Shinde's 'lion' jibe with a post calling some people disloyal dogs. stories.title: 'Major win for India': Vivek Aggarwal elected as FATF vice president
stories.summary: India has achieved a significant leadership role in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) with Vivek Aggarwal elected as its Vice President. This appointment underscores India's commitment to combating money laundering and terrorist financing globally. Aggarwal's extensive experience, including leading India's FATF delegation and heading the Financial Intelligence Unit, will bolster the organization's efforts to secure financial integrity and dismantle illicit financial systems.

stories.title: 'Just being cute, funny': Donald Trump clarifies 'I'm the boss' remark at G7 summit
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has clarified his "I'm the boss" remark at the G7 summit, stating it was a lighthearted joke intended to be funny, not an assertion of authority. He explained the comment arose from the unusual seating arrangement at the summit. Trump's clarification comes amid significant diplomatic developments, including a US-Iran agreement.

stories.title: Falta candidate Jahangir Khan's wife Sarina Bibi arrested in bid to free TMC leader from police custody
stories.summary: West Bengal Police have apprehended Sarina Bibi, wife of former TMC leader Jahangir Khan, for allegedly masterminding an attack on Falta police station. The incident aimed to free Khan from custody. This arrest is part of a wider crackdown on Khan's alleged criminal network, following his own apprehension near the India-Nepal border. Investigations into the attack are ongoing, with further arrests anticipated.

Passengers described being violently thrown, witnessing smoke, and hearing screams as emergency services rushed to the site. The offering will be a primary share sale, with proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and corporate needs, marking a significant value-creation milestone for the company. This move signals a major event for the Indian stock market, with Jio expected to command a valuation exceeding $100 billion.

stories.title: Walking a fundamental right, footpath must for all roads: Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has declared the right to walk a fundamental right, integral to life and free movement. The apex court urged the government to enact a law ensuring well-demarcated footpaths on all roads, prioritizing pedestrian safety over motorized vehicles. This landmark ruling empowers citizens to seek legal recourse for violations and mandates civic bodies to maintain pedestrian infrastructure, transforming urban and rural living.

stories.summary: Pilots' union FIP alleges the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's report on Air India flight 171 omits crucial cockpit warnings of an electrical failure preceding engine loss. stories.title: PM Modi to preside over ceremony to commission 2 warships, one survey vessel into Navy tomorrow

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will preside over the ceremony for the stealth frigate Dunagiri, survey vessel Sanshodhak, and anti-submarine warfare craft Agray. These platforms significantly boost India's blue-water capabilities, coastal defense, and surveying prowess, showcasing the nation's growing shipbuilding prowess with over 75% indigenous content.

The piece argues that despite contributions in technology, medicine, and education, Indians face prejudice regarding civic sense, job competition, and cultural identity. It calls for judgment based on individual actions rather than generalizations, celebrating a rich heritage and resilient spirit.

Only Arvind Sawant, Anil Desai and Rajabhau Waze attended the meeting, reaffirming their loyalty to party chief Uddhav Thackeray.

stories.title: Ex-DRDO scientist accused of sharing secrets with Pakistani agent to face trial
stories.summary: A former DRDO scientist, Pradeep Kurulkar, faces charges in an espionage case, with trial set to begin next month. Accused of sharing classified defence information with a suspected Pakistani intelligence agent, Kurulkar's plea for discharge was rejected. Proceedings will be held in-camera due to the sensitive nature of the Official Secrets Act violations.

NTA to conduct nationwide mock drill on June 20 ahead of NEET-UG re-examination
stories.summary: Ahead of the NEET-UG 2026 re-examination on June 21, the National Testing Agency (NTA) will conduct a nationwide mock drill on June 20. This measure aims to ensure a seamless process for the nearly 23 lakh candidates. The NTA is actively communicating with students, urging them to download fresh admit cards and warning against fraudulent messages.

stories.title: 'Hope Speaker gives us justice': Abhishek Banerjee files disqualification pleas against rebel MPs
stories.summary: Expressing hope that Lok Sabha Om Birla​​​​​​ would "act in accordance with the Constitution," Banerjee said: "The Lok Sabha Speaker is the custodian of the House, not the protector of the government of the day. Every citizen, especially elected representatives, must work within the ambit of the law. Therefore, one has to function according to the provisions laid down in the Constitution."

stories.summary: Donald Trump lauded PM Modi as a "tough cookie" and admired leader, while Meloni refuted Trump's claim of begging for a G7 photo. Speaking to Axios, Trump highlighted their strong personal rapport, even amidst trade tensions. This praise follows their recent G7 meeting, where Trump emphasized the close India-US relationship and PM Modi's formidable negotiating skills, suggesting a trade deal is nearing completion.

stories.title: The great reverse migration: Why India's professionals are leaving Metro cities
stories.summary: A fascinating trend is emerging as Indian professionals increasingly desert sprawling metropolises in favor of tier-2 and tier-3 cities, searching for a richer quality of life. The rising costs of living, extensive travel for work, and the stress of city life are significant forces behind this migration.

The Indian Cultural Centre in Kuala Lumpur acts as a vital hub, fostering a unique, localized Indian cultural identity woven into Malaysia's multi-racial fabric, promoting mutual understanding and shared heritage.

stories.summary: Andy Burnham's decisive Makerfield by-election victory has intensified pressure on Labour leader Sir Keir Starmer. stories.title: Subsidence sparks fear in Jammu & Kashmir village; residents evacuated
stories.summary: Panic spread in Rajouri's Kotli Kalaban village as land subsidence created large cracks. Agricultural fields, roads, and homes suffered damage. District officials evacuated residents from two severely damaged houses. The Geological Survey of India has been called to assess the situation. This follows similar incidents in Doda, Ramban, Reasi, and Poonch districts in recent years.

stories.title: JCO, 3 soldiers hurt in accidental blast along LoC in Jammu & Kashmir’s Rajouri
stories.summary: Four Army personnel, including a JCO and three jawans, were injured in an accidental landmine blast during a patrol near the LoC in Rajouri district. India's high hazard exposure score, especially for extreme heat and air pollution, highlights the urgent need for targeted interventions to protect young lives.

Concerns persist over Iran's military arsenal and its potential to use the strait as leverage in future disputes, even as diplomatic efforts continue.
